bodyMarkdown:
## Converting Hourly to Annual Pay

Whether you're a teacher, a tradie, or an office worker, understanding how your hourly rate translates into an annual salary is essential for budgeting, negotiating, and comparing job offers. The basic formula is straightforward: multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work each week, then by 52 weeks in a year. For a standard full-time position of 38 hours per week, the calculation is:

**Annual gross pay = hourly rate × 38 × 52**

This assumes you work the same hours every week with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, or allowances. If you work part-time or different hours, adjust the weekly figure. For example, a 20-hour week would use 20 instead of 38.

To see your fortnightly pay, simply double your weekly gross amount. This can help with budgeting if you're paid every two weeks.

## State Differences in Ordinary-Time Earnings

Earnings vary across Australian states and territories. According to the Australian Bureau of Statistics (ABS) Average Weekly Earnings for May 2026, full-time adult ordinary-time earnings in New South Wales averaged $2,108.80 per week. This is an average across all occupations and industries, not a median for any specific job such as a high school teacher. If you are researching the **high school teacher salary nsw**, keep in mind that the actual figure for a teacher depends on their classification, experience, and the specific award or enterprise agreement. The NSW average of $2,108.80 per week provides a broad reference point, but it is not a job-specific median.

For comparison, the national full-time adult ordinary-time average was $2,083.70 per week. State differences reflect local labour markets, cost of living, and industry mix. When using our [reference tables](/data), you can see these averages, but always check your own award or contract for your exact rate.

## National Minimum Wage and Award Rates

The Fair Work Commission sets the National Minimum Wage each year. From 1 July 2026, the minimum is $26.44 per hour, or $1,004.90 per week for 38 hours. Casual employees receive a 25% loading, making their minimum $33.05 per hour. This loading compensates for the lack of paid leave entitlements.

However, most employees are covered by an award or registered agreement that sets higher minimum rates. For example, teachers in NSW are typically covered by the Crown Employees (Teachers in Schools and Related Employees) Salaries and Conditions Award. Award rates are legally enforceable and often exceed the national minimum. You can find award pay guides on the Fair Work Ombudsman website. Use our [pay guides](/blog) to understand how awards apply to your situation.

## Casual Loading and Superannuation

If you work casually, your employer must pay a 25% loading on top of the base hourly rate. This is not optional – it's a legal requirement under the Fair Work Act. When using our [the timesheet](/), you can check a box to add the 25% casual loading. Do not type a rate that already includes loading; the tool adds it for you.

Superannuation is paid on top of your ordinary earnings. The super guarantee rate is 12% for 2026–27, applied to your gross pay up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year. For example, if your annual salary is $80,000, your employer contributes an extra $9,600 to your super fund. This is not deducted from your take-home pay. Learn more about [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging).

## Tax and Take-Home Pay

Your gross annual salary is not what you take home. The Australian Taxation Office (ATO) applies progressive tax rates for residents in 2026–27:
- Nil on income up to $18,200
- 15% on income from $18,201 to $45,000
- 30% on income from $45,001 to $135,000
- 37% on income from $135,001 to $190,000
- 45% on income above $190,000

Plus a Medicare levy of 2% (with possible reductions for low-income earners). The tax-free threshold is included. Note: the Medicare levy reduction thresholds used here are from 2025–26 as the 2026–27 figures were not confirmed. HELP repayments, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not included in this estimate.

To estimate your after-tax pay, use our [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) guide or the [hourly conversion](/topics/hourly-conversion) tool.

## Using the Timesheet for Your Own Rate

The easiest way to see your annual, fortnightly, and weekly figures is to use [the timesheet](/). Enter your base hourly rate (without casual loading), select your hours per week (default 38), and the tool will calculate gross annual pay, tax, Medicare, and super. If you are casual, tick the casual loading box to add 25% on top. The tool uses the latest Fair Work and ATO figures.

Remember: this is an estimate. It assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. For a precise determination of your pay, consult your employer, award, or a qualified accountant.

## Conclusion

Whether you're comparing a **high school teacher salary nsw** with other states, or checking your own hourly rate, the conversion formula is simple. Use the ABS averages as a guide, but always refer to your specific award or agreement for your exact pay. Our tools and guides help you make sense of the numbers, from gross annual to take-home pay, including super and tax. Start with [the timesheet](/), or explore [average pay](/topics/average-pay) and [job pay](/topics/job-pay) for more context.
